toLevel5.correctExplanation: A graph that drops steadily clearly shows the value going down across the years it covers.

distractors.answer: The claim is correct because every graph in every country shows no change in every year of any life today at all stages
distractors.explanation: Many graphs show clear change; the no-change claim is wrong.

distractors.answer: The claim is correct because line graphs never show any direction in any country at any stage of any year today at all
distractors.explanation: Line graphs are widely used to show direction in data.

distractors.answer: The claim is correct because every dropping line in every economic investigation always shows no change today at all
distractors.explanation: Dropping lines show falling values, not no change.

toLevel5.question: A claim is made that 'analysing text in a business report is a recognised inquiry skill'. Which response best fits?
toLevel5.correct: The claim is well supported because identifying key findings and summarising conclusions from text is widely taught at this level
toLevel5.correctExplanation: Identifying key findings and summarising conclusions from text is widely taught as an inquiry skill at this level.

distractors.answer: The claim is unsupported because no inquiry skill in any country at any stage of any year of any life today at all stages
distractors.explanation: Inquiry skills are closely linked to many subjects.

distractors.answer: The claim is unsupported because every investigator always relies only on graphs and never on any text in any year today
distractors.explanation: Many investigators analyse text alongside graphs.

distractors.answer: The claim is unsupported because business reports always block every inquiry in every country at every stage today at all
distractors.explanation: Business reports support, rather than block, inquiry.

toLevel5.question: Two friends compare an investigation that uses graphs and one that uses only text. Which evaluation best fits?
toLevel5.correct: Both graphs and text contribute to investigation; combining them often produces stronger analysis than either alone
toLevel5.correctExplanation: Both graphs and text contribute to investigation; combining them often produces stronger analysis than either alone.

distractors.answer: The two investigations always produce identical results in every country at every stage of any year today at all stages
distractors.explanation: Graphs and text often produce different but complementary investigations.

distractors.answer: The graph-only investigation always produces stronger results than the text-only investigation in every case today at all
distractors.explanation: Graph-only and text-only investigations both have strengths and weaknesses.

distractors.answer: The two investigations have no link to any economic issue in any country at any stage of any year today at any time
distractors.explanation: Both investigations are linked to economic issues.

toLevel5.question: A claim is made that 'a supply and demand graph can show how a tax change affects price and quantity'. Which response best fits?
toLevel5.correct: The claim is well supported because shifting one curve to model the tax shows the new equilibrium price and quantity
toLevel5.correctExplanation: Shifting one curve to model the tax shows the new equilibrium price and quantity in standard analysis.

distractors.answer: The claim is unsupported because no graph ever shows any tax effect in any country at any stage of any year today at all
distractors.explanation: Supply and demand graphs are widely used to show tax effects.

distractors.answer: The claim is unsupported because every supply and demand graph always blocks every analysis in every country today at all
distractors.explanation: Supply and demand graphs support, rather than block, analysis.

distractors.answer: The claim is unsupported because every tax change always has identical effects in every market regardless of the graph
distractors.explanation: Tax changes have different effects in different markets; the graph helps reveal this.

toLevel5.question: A claim is made that 'graph and model skills support decisions in many areas of daily life'. Which response best fits?
toLevel5.correct: The claim is well supported because graph and model skills help interpret news, government reports, and many decisions
toLevel5.correctExplanation: Graph and model skills help interpret news, government reports, and many decisions across daily life.

distractors.answer: The claim is unsupported because graph and model skills have no link to any decision in any country at any stage today
distractors.explanation: These skills are closely linked to many decisions.

distractors.answer: The claim is unsupported because every decision always uses identical skills regardless of any graph in every year today
distractors.explanation: Decisions vary widely in the skills they use; treating all as identical is wrong.

distractors.answer: The claim is unsupported because graph and model skills always block every everyday decision in every country today at all
distractors.explanation: Graph and model skills support, rather than block, everyday decisions.

toLevel5.question: A student claims that 'an economic model and a graph are the same thing'. Which response best fits?
toLevel5.correct: The claim is misleading because a model is a simplified description of relationships while a graph shows data visually
toLevel5.correctExplanation: A model is a simplified description of relationships; a graph is one visual way to show data or model output.

distractors.answer: The claim is correct because every economic model and every graph are identical in every detail in every year today at all
distractors.explanation: Models and graphs differ; treating them as identical is wrong.

distractors.answer: The claim is correct because no investigator has ever distinguished a model from a graph in any country at any stage today
distractors.explanation: Many investigators distinguish models from graphs in their work.

distractors.answer: The claim is correct because every graph always replaces every model in every country at every stage of any year today at all
distractors.explanation: Graphs and models often work together; one does not always replace the other.

toLevel5.question: A claim is made that 'building, reading, and drawing conclusions from graphs supports economic investigation'. Which response best fits?
toLevel5.correct: The claim is well supported because these three skills together cover the main stages of working with economic data
toLevel5.correctExplanation: Building, reading, and drawing conclusions from graphs cover the main stages of working with economic data.

distractors.answer: The claim is unsupported because none of these three skills ever helps any investigator in any country at any stage today
distractors.explanation: These three skills help many investigators.

distractors.answer: The claim is unsupported because every researcher always skips every one of these three skills in every investigation today
distractors.explanation: Many investigators use these three skills regularly.

distractors.answer: The claim is unsupported because random outcomes always produce stronger investigations than these three skills today at all
distractors.explanation: Random outcomes do not produce stronger investigations than structured skills.
